citations.quote: QFITLIA is indicated for routine prophylaxis to prevent or reduce the frequency of bleeding episodes in adult and pediatric patients aged 12 years and older with hemophilia A or B with or without factor VIII or IX inhibitors.

target_moa.text: A double-stranded siRNA that degrades antithrombin (AT) mRNA via RNA interference on the SERPINC1 gene, reducing plasma AT levels; AT normally inactivates thrombin (factor IIa) and factor Xa, so lowering it rebalances hemostasis.

citations.quote: Fitusiran (proprietary name QFITLIA), a new molecular entity, is a double-stranded small interfering ribonucleic acid (siRNA) that causes degradation of antithrombin (AT) messenger RNA (mRNA) through RNA interference, reducing plasma AT levels. AT is a serine protease inhibitor that inactivates thrombin (factor IIa) and factor Xa, along with other enzymes in the coagulation system.
Fitusiran inhibits hepatocyte AT production through RNA interference on the *SERPINC1* gene
Fitusiran (proprietary name QFITLIA), a new molecular entity, is a double-stranded small interfering ribonucleic acid (siRNA)

key_safety.text: Most common adverse reactions (≥10%): viral infection (29%), nasopharyngitis (26%), and bacterial infection (11%). Serious risks include thromboembolic events and gallbladder disease (boxed warning) and hepatotoxicity.

citations.quote: The most common adverse reactions (\ge 10\%) were viral infection (29%), nasopharyngitis (26%), and bacterial infection (11%).

Fitusiran has serious risks of thromboembolic events and gallbladder disease (including cholecystitis, cholelithiasis, and the need for cholecystectomy in some patients). These risks and mitigation recommendations will be described in a boxed warning. Hepatotoxicity is also a serious risk that will be described in a Warning and Precaution

detail.text: WARNING: THROMBOTIC EVENTS AND ACUTE AND RECURRENT GALLBLADDER DISEASE — serious thrombotic events (risk factors include persistent AT activity <15%, 80 mg once monthly dosing, indwelling venous catheters, post-operative setting) and acute/recurrent gallbladder disease, some requiring cholecystectomy or with complications such as pancreatitis.

citations.quote: ## WARNING: THROMBOTIC EVENTS AND ACUTE AND RECURRENT GALLBLADDER DISEASE

Serious thrombotic events have occurred in QFITLIA-treated patients with risk factors for thromboembolism including persistent antithrombin (AT) activity less than 15%, use of QFITLIA 80 mg once monthly, presence of indwelling venous catheters, and in the post-operative setting when bleed management guidelines were not followed.

Acute and recurrent gallbladder disease, including cholelithiasis and cholecystitis have occurred in QFITLIA-treated patients, some of whom required cholecystectomy or had complications (e.g., pancreatitis) related to gallbladder disease.

detail.text: INNOVANCE Antithrombin assay, FDA-authorized as a companion diagnostic to measure AT activity and adjust fitusiran dosing to target AT activity of 15-35%.

citations.quote: The Center for Devices and Radiological Health evaluated the INNOVANCE Antithrombin assay that the Applicant is proposing for monitoring AT activity. This assay will be FDA-authorized as a Companion Diagnostic on the date of drug approval.
